propositions: Defect review (7–21 Aug 2026) identified 56 bugs caused by duplicated decision logic replicated 2–7 times across codebase, with fixes landing in one copy while twins remain broken, creating multi-ticket families (sidecar keying ×3, git_adapter ×3, nested-pytest ×3, comment key/send ×5, compaction ×6).

Consolidation children must collapse duplicated computations into single shared modules, preserve all current pinned observable behaviour via named pinning tests, and include construct-uniqueness guards that assert exactly one implementation exists (not how it works) using distinctive atom conjunctions or AST shapes with explicit escape markers.

Eight consolidation children (StorePaths, stamped lock, cascade, replacement walk, token twins, fit_for_send, nested pytest, gate policy) have merged; acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 are empirically unsatisfiable as written because consolidation work legitimately violates both proxies (test deletion occurs when removing duplicated blocks; net lines are +241 across 8 children due to documentation overhead).

AC2 proxy (tests-only additions) fails for 6 of 8 merged children; actual intent (no pinned observable behaviour changes) holds for all; test deletions occur when consolidation removes duplicated helper blocks and re-points references at consolidated owner.

AC3 criterion (net non-test lines negative) measured +241 across 8 merged children and trending further positive; extractions relocate duplicated bodies and must document rationale, so owner modules cost more than call-site savings; only 3 of 8 are net-negative, none by >13 lines.

Thirteen consolidation children and nine hardening children remain open; close is blocked by 4 unchecked acceptance criteria, two of which are empirically false as proxy metrics rather than evidence of incorrect work; operator decision required to revise AC2/AC3 to state actual guarantees (one implementation per construct + no silent behaviour change) plus evidence comment, or apply alternative resolution method.
